terms.definition: A scalar $\lambda$ for which a square matrix $A$ has a nonzero vector $v$ satisfying $Av=\lambda v$. It describes the scale factor applied to an eigenvector direction, including zero and negative factors.

A nonzero vector whose direction is preserved by a specified linear transformation, up to scaling or reversal. Multiplying an eigenvector by any nonzero scalar gives another eigenvector for the same eigenvalue.

The null space of $A-\lambda I$ for a given eigenvalue $\lambda$. It includes the zero vector and every eigenvector associated with that eigenvalue, so it is a subspace rather than a set containing only eigenvectors.
The polynomial $\det(A-\lambda I)$, using the sign convention in this article. Its roots are the eigenvalues, counted with their algebraic multiplicities.
A square matrix that is not invertible. Equivalently, its determinant is zero and its null space contains a nonzero vector; for a square matrix, this means zero is an eigenvalue.
A representation $P^{-1}AP=\Lambda$ in which $P$ is invertible and $\Lambda$ is diagonal. It exists exactly when the matrix has a full set of linearly independent eigenvectors.

Two square matrices are similar when one can be written as $P^{-1}AP$ for an invertible matrix $P$. Similar matrices have the same characteristic polynomial and eigenvalues, though equal eigenvalues alone do not imply similarity.

A matrix summarizing variances of individual variables on its diagonal and pairwise covariances off the diagonal. For real-valued data it is symmetric, and its eigenvectors and eigenvalues describe directions and amounts of variation.

A CSV data record whose number of parsed fields differs from the number of header fields. `csv-profile` records its one-based logical CSV record number, counting the header as record 1, not its physical text-line number, and skips it when computing per-column missing and numeric summaries.

A numeric representation such as `NaN`, positive infinity, or negative infinity that is not a finite real number. `csv-profile` excludes parsed nonfinite values from numeric counts and summary statistics.
